evidence: The XRR was performed using a PANalytical X'Pert PRO X-ray diffractometer with Cu Kα source. In the GIXRD, the incidence angle was 1°. Specimens for transmission electron microscopy (TEM) were prepared with the lift-out method in a FEI Quanta 3D 200i focused ion beam (FIB)-scanning electron microscope (SEM), i.e., FIB-SEM dual beam microscope. Bright-field TEM images were taken with a FEI Tecnai F-20 microscope operated at 200 kV. EDX was also applied for the measurements on the residual chlorine content in the solid films by a Hitachi S-4800 scanning electron microscope (SEM) equipped with an Oxford INCA 350 EDX spectrometer. The thicknesses of the films were determined from reflectance spectra measured within a wavelength range of 380–1100 nm using a Hitachi U2000 spectrophotometer and applying a fitting method developed by Ylilammi and Ranta-aho. The composition of selected as-deposited and annealed samples was determined by Time-of-Flight Elastic Recoil Analysis (ToF-ERDA), using 35 MeV 127I7+ beam. The measurement geometry was 15 ± 25° (scattering/detection angle 40°, incident angle 15° from sample surface). For electrical measurements, Al/Ti/ZrO2/TiN/Si/Al and Al/Ti/ZrO2/Si/Al capacitors were constructed with the capacitor area of 0.204 mm 2. The capacitance–voltage (C–V) curves were measured using an HP4284A precision LCR meter in the a.c. frequency range of 1 kHz – 1 MHz, applying a series capacitance–dissipation (Cs–D) measurement mode with a bias voltage step of 0.1 V and a trigger delay of 0.5 s. For current–voltage measurements a Keithley 2400 source meter was used applying stair step voltage with a voltage step of 0.1 V and 0.5 s delay.
